claim_text: We maintained our ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications through the year and recorded no significant environmental incidents or non-compliances— a record we are determined to uphold.
metric_name: ISO 14001 certification status; ISO 45001 certification status; significant environmental incidents
context_text:
In 2025 we maintained our ISO 45001 certification at the Syama and Mako operations：
In 2025, we maintained our ISO:14001 certification at Mako
and are awaiting re-certification at Syama in Q2 2026. 
In 2025, Syama and Mako only reported minor incidents,
the majority related to the management of surface water quality and hydrocarbon spills, with localised impacts. We recorded no significant environmental incidents or regulatory non-compliances.
label: Suspected Greenwash
rationale_short: The no-significant-incidents part is supported, but the ISO 14001 part is contradicted because the report states Syama was awaiting re-certification in Q2 2026.
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertions are (1) that ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications were maintained throughout the year and (2) that there were no significant environmental incidents or non-compliances during the year. No evidence fields were provided to substantiate either the certification status (e.g., valid certificates, audit dates/results, scope) or the incident/non-compliance record (e.g., reported incident counts, definitions of “significant,” compliance findings). With no substantive evidence, the claim is not meaningfully verified.
